# DarkSlide v1.3.0

DarkSlide 1.3.0 redesigns the editor around how film is actually scanned: as rolls of frames, not single images. Everything you adjust now lives in one inspector driven by a tool rail, open frames sit in a filmstrip you can select from, and exporting several frames keeps each frame's own edits. The design builds on ideas from Durieux's ([@tdurieux](https://github.com/tdurieux)) [DarkSlide fork](https://github.com/tdurieux/DarkSlide) and the [redesign mockups](https://github.com/kilianvivien/DarkSlide/tree/main/design/mockups). Conversion color output is unchanged from 1.2.4.

## Highlights

- **Tool rail and one inspector.** Develop, Curves, Film profiles, Crop, Dust and Export are icons on a rail at the left, each with a number shortcut (1–6). They all open in the same panel, including film profiles, custom presets and rolls, which used to live in a separate right-hand panel. Choose the open tool again to collapse the panel and give the image the full width.
- **Filmstrip instead of tabs.** Open frames appear as numbered thumbnails under the image, each showing whether it has a film base, a crop and unsaved edits. Thumbnails come from previews DarkSlide already rendered, so the strip costs no extra processing. Use ← and → to move between frames.
- **Work on several frames at once.** ⌘/Ctrl-click or Shift-click frames to select them. The selection bar can sync the current frame's look to the others (each keeps its own crop, rotation, level and dust repairs, and each can be undone), stabilize their crops, or export them.
- **Export frames with their own edits.** The Export panel starts with a choice of This frame, Selected or All, and one Export button with progress and Cancel. Every frame keeps its own look and file name; the panel's format, size and colour settings apply to all of them. ⌘⇧E opens it.
- **Convert Files & Contact Sheets.** The old batch export is now focused on what it does best: applying one shared recipe to scans you have not opened, and laying out contact sheets. It opens from the Export panel.
- **Switchable adjustment groups.** Develop is organized into Tone, Range, White Balance and Color, each with an on/off switch to compare with and without that group. Switched-off groups keep their values, and the film stock's own calibration still applies.
- **Image toolbar.** A floating toolbar under the image switches between the converted image and the negative and rotates, crops and zooms. The header now shows the open file, its position in the roll and its size.
- **Smoother curves and steadier shortcuts.** Curve drags update once per frame instead of on every mouse move, and the undo step records the final curve. Shortcuts match modifiers exactly and never fire twice when a focused control already handled the key.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Action | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Develop / Curves / Film profiles / Crop / Dust / Export | 1 – 6 |
| Toggle film profiles | P |
| Toggle crop overlay | C |
| Before / after | \ |
| Previous / next frame | ← → |
| Clear frame selection | Esc |
| Export several frames | ⌘⇧E |

The full list is in Settings → Shortcuts.

## Desktop Downloads

GitHub Actions builds and attaches installers for each supported desktop platform:

- macOS: universal Apple Silicon and Intel `.dmg`
- Windows: `.msi` and NSIS `.exe`
- Linux: `.deb` and `.AppImage`

## Installation Notes

- macOS builds are not notarized. On first launch, macOS may require opening the app through System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
- Windows and Linux builds are unsigned.

## Validation

Type-checking, ESLint, all tests, the production web build and the Rust tests passed. New coverage includes the tool rail and shortcuts, filmstrip selection rules and actions, look syncing that preserves per-frame geometry, per-frame export with shared output settings, thumbnail capture, adjustment groups rendering identically on the CPU and GPU paths, curve-edit undo, and shortcut modifier matching.
